assumptions: Bootstrap: seed 20261027, 1000 resamples of (x, y) pairs with replacement; the interval is the 5th and 95th percentile by nearest rank on the sorted slopes (index floor(p x (resamples - 1))). ASSUMPTION.
Seasons are meteorological: DJF, MAM, JJA, SON. ASSUMPTION.
Hours are Mountain prevailing clock time of the hour start, from the UTC start with written-out DST dates; the repeated 1am on Nov 2 2025 joins hour 1. ASSUMPTION.
Bad-hour rules (ASSUMPTION): demand missing or at most 0; forecast missing or at most 0; demand outside 0.5x to 1.5x the forecast.

marginal_co2.unit: g CO2 per kWh (slope in t/MWh x 1,000)

x.generated: hourly change in EIA net generation, MW
x.consumed: hourly change in EIA demand, MW

y.generated: hourly change in EIA CO2 emissions generated, t
y.consumed: hourly change in consumed CO2, t = co2_cons_lb_kwh x demand_mw x 1000 / 2204.62262

sources.license: Public domain; credit the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

caveats: EIA's hourly CO2 is fuel-type generation times EIA emission factors, so the slope measures fuel-mix response, not plant heat rates.
PACE exports in most hours, and midday curtailment is invisible in net generation, which can bias midday factors.
Method after Siler-Evans, Azevedo and Morgan 2012 (citation UNVERIFIED, not opened).

sources.license: Public domain; credit the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

caveats: Residual = EIA-930 day-ahead demand forecast minus reported demand; positive means over-forecast.

price_response.x: net load, MW (CAISO SLD_FCST day-ahead load forecast minus EDAM day-ahead solar and wind forecast, as in the bundle)
price_response.net_load_basis: CAISO SLD_FCST day-ahead load forecast minus EDAM day-ahead solar and wind forecast, as in the bundle
